> **AI governance, architecture principles & disruption (incl. power-cut) recovery for any software project**, extracted from production development, with documentation and regression-shielded workflows.

---

## ⚡ 30-Second Cold-Start Quick Reference

> **Orientation Contract**: verified commands and prerequisites below.

- **Runtime Prerequisites**: Python 3.10+ (standard library only; no pip dependencies) and `git`.
- **Canonical Regression Shield Gate**:
  ```bash
  python -m unittest discover tests
  ```
  *(100% test pass required before staging or committing).*

### 🛠️ Core Operational Command Matrix

| **Manage Projects**| `python aikit.py <cmd>`| `new`, `attach`, `list`, `status`, `check`, `fix` (ADR-119..124)|
| **Run Regression Suite**| `python scripts/check_test_budgets.py`| Both tiers pass; per-test average <=10ms unit, <=350ms integration|
| **Run One Tier**| `python -m unittest tests.test_kit` / `python -m unittest tests.test_integration`| Isolates a failing tier|
| **Synchronize IDE Rules**| `python scripts/sync_principles.py`| <=1,750 est. tokens/target incl. a reserved 300-token Tier 1B|

They never enter a Tier 1 file: `python aikit.py status <name>` and `resume <name>` print them, and the project's guidelines gate rejects a malformed rule or one worded to override a principle. They rank below Tier 1A and Tier 1B (PRINCIPLE-000 R6).

IDs MUST NOT be renumbered or reused. To read a principle, search for the literal text `### PRINCIPLE-NNN:` with any text-search tool and read from that line up to the next line that starts with `### `, `## ` or `---`. Agents MUST NOT rely on remembered line numbers.

On a Track C task (PRINCIPLE-002 R3) the agent MUST evaluate the Pre-Flight checklist before its first file edit of the task. On Track B and Track C tasks it MUST evaluate the Post-Flight checklist before committing. Track A tasks evaluate neither. The agent MUST NOT paste either checklist into the conversation; it reports only failed or skipped items, one line each naming the principle ID, and when nothing failed it reports `checklists passed`. content.text:
Yes, this can work without building an iPhone app. I'm checking with you before I write code, because it's a different project from the UI-to-code tool we started with.

**How it would work:** your wife's iPhone already has Apple's **Shortcuts** app, so nothing needs to be installed.
- **On the PC:** a small server I build. It stores her photos in date folders, skips duplicates, and has a clean gallery page she can open in Safari and add to her home screen like an app.
- **On the iPhone:** a Shortcuts automation such as "when the phone starts charging at home". It finds the photos added since the last run and sends them to the PC. Since iOS 17 it can run without asking her each time.

**What it can't do:**
- An iPhone web page can't read the photo library in the background. Shortcuts is the only way to make it automatic without an app.
- It syncs over your home Wi-Fi only. Reaching the PC from outside the house would need something like Tailscale, which is an app.
- Big videos may need several runs, because Shortcuts limits how long one run can take.
- iPhone photos are in HEIC format. I'd keep the originals, but showing previews in the gallery needs the `Pillow` + `pillow-heif` libraries. Without them, HEIC photos appear as placeholders.

**My plan:** a new project called `photo-harbor`, built in Python with a hand-built front end. Uploads will need a secret key, and the repo will include step-by-step instructions for setting up the Shortcut.

Should I go ahead with this instead of the UI-to-code tool? And is home-Wi-Fi-only sync OK?
i want it to put photos to my pc when it is on the wifi with the same network. what can we do

Yes. iOS can start a Shortcut when the iPhone connects to your home Wi-Fi, so photos would go to the PC automatically whenever she is at home.

**Three triggers:**
1. **Joining your home Wi-Fi.** When she gets home, the iPhone sends everything new since the last sync.
2. **Plugging in to charge.** Photos she takes while already at home get sent overnight.
3. **A few set times a day (optional),** for example 12:00, 18:00 and 22:00, to catch anything in between.

Before uploading, each run checks the Wi-Fi name. If she isn't on your home network, it stops quietly, so it never tries to reach the PC from outside.

**What each sync does:** it finds the photos and videos added since the last successful sync and sends the originals to the PC. The PC confirms each file and skips anything it already has, and the iPhone only records the sync time once the upload succeeds. If the PC is off, nothing is lost: it just catches up the next time.

**Setup:**
- **PC:** run one command once, then allow it in Windows Firewall when Windows asks (I'll document both).
- **iPhone:** I'll give you an importable Shortcut plus 2 minutes of setup steps. She sets each automation to "Run Immediately" so it never asks her.
- **Gallery:** an `http://<pc-ip>:8642` page that works on the iPhone and the PC, with photos grouped by day.

**Limits:**
- The PC has to be on and awake.
- Very long videos may take a couple of runs to finish.

Shall I start building it as the `photo-harbor` project?
PC can be stay awake, would it sync the photos to my pc and remove from the photos app?

Yes, with two limits that come from iOS, not from my design.

**What works:** after a sync, the Shortcut can delete from the iPhone the photos the PC has confirmed it received in full. Only photos the PC has acknowledged get deleted; anything that failed or is half-uploaded stays on the phone.

**What iOS enforces:**
1. **iOS always asks before deleting.** It shows "Allow deleting N photos?", and no setting turns that off. Syncing stays fully automatic, but deleting needs one tap from her. We can make that tap rare: for example, she runs a "Free up space" shortcut once a week and taps Delete once.
2. **Deleted photos go to "Recently Deleted" for 30 days** and still use space until it's emptied (Photos → Albums → Recently Deleted → Delete All).

**My suggestion:** keep the last 30 days of photos on the phone and only remove older ones the PC already has. She can still show recent photos to people, and space gets freed steadily.

**Two more things:**
- **iCloud Photos:** if it's turned on, deleting on the iPhone also deletes the photo from iCloud and her other devices. That's usually what you want here, but she should know.
- **The PC becomes the only copy.** I'd add a nightly copy to a second drive or USB disk; the server can do that itself. A disk failure would otherwise lose everything.

Should I build it this way: automatic sync on home Wi-Fi, a weekly one-tap cleanup that removes confirmed photos older than 30 days, and an optional nightly backup copy?
so how do we know what is on the pc or not

The PC is the record. Before deleting anything, the iPhone asks the PC about each specific photo and only deletes it if the PC says yes.

**Each photo gets a fingerprint.** Shortcuts has a built-in "Generate Hash" action that turns a file's contents into a SHA-256 code. Two files share that code only if they are byte-for-byte identical. It doesn't depend on the file name, which matters because iPhone names like IMG_1234 start over after 9999.

**When a photo is synced:**
1. The iPhone sends the photo together with its fingerprint.
2. The PC saves it, recomputes the fingerprint from the saved file, and checks that the two match.
3. Only if they match does the PC add it to its list of received photos and answer "stored". A photo cut off by a dropped Wi-Fi connection fails this check and is sent again next time.

**When cleaning up:**
1. The Shortcut picks the photos on the phone that are older than 30 days.
2. It asks the PC "do you have this fingerprint?" for each one.
3. The PC answers yes only if the file is still on its disk and its contents still match. Deleted or damaged files get "no".
4. Only photos with a "yes" go into the delete list, then iOS asks her to confirm.

The check happens fresh at cleanup time, so if a photo went missing from the PC, the phone keeps its copy.

**You can also check it yourself:** the gallery page will have a status view showing the last sync time, how many photos are stored, and any photos that are on the phone but not yet on the PC.

**One caveat:** fingerprinting very large videos on the iPhone can be slow. If it turns out to be too slow during testing, videos would fall back to matching on date taken, file size and duration, and I'd tell you if that happens.

Should I start building `photo-harbor` with this design?
Start.

This operational runbook provides the unified command matrix for driving AIKit across all supported agent host clients (Antigravity, Claude, OpenCode, Cursor, Copilot, Windsurf, Cline) under **PRINCIPLE-009 R7** (Pluggable Host Architecture) and **PRINCIPLE-017 R2** (Cross-IDE Synchronization).

---

## 🌐 Host Client Operation Matrix

- **Antigravity**: Native chat harness. Discovers this skill via `.agents/skills/aikit/SKILL.md` and rule files in `.agents/rules/`.
- **Claude (Code CLI / Desktop)**: Reads `CLAUDE.md` automatically on startup. Discovers this skill natively via `.claude/skills/aikit/SKILL.md`. Executes kit commands directly via terminal tool calls.
- **OpenCode**: Runs headless subagent profiles (`architect`, `coder`, `tester`, etc.) via `opencode run --standalone` and slash commands via `opencode.jsonc`.
- **Cursor / VS Code / Windsurf / Cline**: Loads `.cursorrules`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, `.windsurfrules`, `.clinerules`. Runs terminal commands.
- **State SSOT**: All clients interact with workspace state strictly through `python scripts/disruption_recovery.py` and `.agents/task_ledger.json` (a project's: `.aikit/task_ledger.json`).

---

## 🧱 Projects: Building Software Other Than AIKit (PRINCIPLE-011 R8)
The user's software lives in its own project, never in AIKit's tree:
```bash
python aikit.py list                 # which projects exist
python aikit.py new <name> --description "<10-350 chars>" [--topic <t>]...  # projects/<name>/: own repo, .aikit/ memory, AGPL-3.0 LICENSE, Built with AIKit badge; topic aikit always added; --publish (needs --description) uploads only these starter files, only when the user asks
python aikit.py attach <path>        # an existing folder: adds .aikit/ memory and an AIKit Integrated badge under its README title (uncommitted)
python aikit.py status <name>        # its task, changes, latest decision and its gates
python aikit.py check <name>         # its Phase 4: tests, stack gates, hygiene, guidelines, secret scan; exit 0 to commit; never pushes, add --push only when push delivery is authorized (PRINCIPLE-018 R4)
python aikit.py guideline <name> "<rule>" --source user   # a project rule, below the principles
python aikit.py publish <name> [--public]   # its own GitHub repo with project.json's description and topics; only when the user asks
python aikit.py fix <name>           # self-heals memory, cleans stale temp buffers, syncs codebase map
python aikit.py checkpoint <name>    # disruption checkpoint on the project ledger; --agent <host>:<session> names you
python aikit.py resume <name>        # disruption resume on the project
python aikit.py complete <name>      # mark project task complete; another agent's task needs --take-over
python aikit.py clean <name>         # clean dangling project buffers
```
- Request names no single project: ask which one, or the name of a new one, before writing code.
- Before writing code in a project, read its guidelines (`status` or `resume` prints them): its own rules, which add to the principles and never override one (PRINCIPLE-000 R6). When the user states a lasting rule for the project, record it with `aikit guideline`.
- In the steps below, project work replaces the repository with the project: use the cockpit subcommands above, or add `--workspace <project path>` to every `disruption_recovery.py` command, write ADRs in `<project>/.aikit/decisions.md`, stage and commit inside the project, and run `python aikit.py check <name>` as Phase 4. `aikit fix <name>` self-heals project memory and cleans temporary buffers. AIKit's other gates are for changes to AIKit only.
- The project check runs the built-in hygiene scan of its source and static assets: mark a deliberate finding `hygiene: allow <reason>` on its own line or the line directly above it. After the check passes, record the checklist outcome (`checklists: passed`, or the failed or skipped item IDs) in the task's latest checkpoint description before the commit (PRINCIPLE-001 R8, PRINCIPLE-011 R8).

A dependency-free, local-first expense ledger for the terminal. Record what you spend, list it,
and see where the money went. Everything stays in one readable JSON file on your machine.

## ⚡ 30-Second Cold-Start Quick Reference

- **Runtime Prerequisites**: Python 3.10 or newer (standard library only; no third-party packages)
- **Canonical Regression Shield Gate**:
  ```bash
  python -m unittest discover
  ```
- **Try it now** (under 10 seconds, from this folder):
  ```bash
  python -m tally add 12.50 --category food --note lunch
  python -m tally add 3.00 --category transport
  python -m tally list
  python -m tally edit 1 --amount 13.00
  python -m tally remove 2
  python -m tally summary
  ```

### 🛠️ AIKit Commands (run from the AIKit folder)

| Role | Command |
|---|---|
| Status, task and gates | `python aikit.py status tally` |
| Phase 4: every gate | `python aikit.py check tally` |
| Repair memory and map, then check | `python aikit.py fix tally` |
| Resume an interrupted task | `python aikit.py resume tally` |

## 💡 How It Works

- **Money is integer cents.** Amounts are parsed with `Decimal`, never floats, so totals stay exact.
- **One ledger file.** `tally.json` (or `--db <path>`) holds `{"version": 1, "expenses": [...]}`.
- **Stable ids.** `list` shows each id, and `edit` or `remove` takes it. A new id is one past the
  highest remaining id, so deleting the newest entry frees that id for the next entry.
- **Crash-safe writes.** Each save keeps a `.bak`, writes a temporary file, fsyncs it, then
  replaces the ledger atomically. A transient Windows sharing violation is retried; any other
  replace failure is reported at once. A failed backup or directory fsync prints a warning. A
  malformed file is quarantined and the backup is restored.
- **One writer at a time.** Read-modify-write operations hold an advisory `.lock` with a 3-second
  wait; a lock older than 30 seconds is broken.
- **Date and month filtering.** `list` and `summary` accept `--month YYYY-MM` or `--from` and `--to`
  to view and total spending within specific periods.
- **Clear failures.** Every user error prints `Error:`, `Why:` and `Fix:`, and exits 1.

### Commands

```text
python -m tally [--db PATH] add AMOUNT [--category NAME] [--note TEXT] [--date YYYY-MM-DD]
python -m tally [--db PATH] edit ID [--amount AMOUNT] [--category NAME] [--note TEXT] [--date YYYY-MM-DD]
python -m tally [--db PATH] remove ID
python -m tally [--db PATH] list [--category NAME] [--from YYYY-MM-DD] [--to YYYY-MM-DD] [--month YYYY-MM]
python -m tally [--db PATH] summary [--from YYYY-MM-DD] [--to YYYY-MM-DD] [--month YYYY-MM]
```

## 📦 What's Inside
### ADR-003: Edit and remove by the id `list` shows
- **Date**: 2026-10-19
- **Status**: Accepted
- **Context**: The bootstrap only appended. Correcting a typo or deleting a duplicate meant
  hand-editing `tally.json`, the one file the atomic store and backup exist to protect.
- **Decision**: Add `edit ID` and `remove ID`. `edit` changes any subset of `--amount`,
  `--category`, `--note` and `--date`, and refuses a call with no field. Both commands run through
  `StateStore.update`, so they hold the same lock, keep the same `.bak` and replace the ledger
  atomically. A missing id fails with the Error/Why/Fix triad. New ids are one past the highest
  remaining id, so deleting the newest entry frees its id for the next entry; every entry that
  remains keeps its id.
- **Consequences**: Mistakes are fixed without touching the JSON. The previous version stays in
  `.bak` until the next write. Because ids are derived from the live file, an id is a handle to a
  current entry, not a permanent historical key; a future schema that persists a counter would be
  the migration path if permanent identity is needed.

### ADR-004: Date range and month filtering for list and summary
- **Date**: 2026-10-19
- **Status**: Accepted
- **Context**: `list` only allowed filtering by category, and `summary` always totaled all recorded
  expenses across the lifetime of the ledger. Users need to inspect and summarize expenses for
  specific periods, especially by month or custom date windows.
- **Decision**: Add `--from YYYY-MM-DD`, `--to YYYY-MM-DD`, and `--month YYYY-MM` (`-m`) options
  to both `list` and `summary`. `--month` resolves to inclusive start and end dates based on the
  calendar month (handling leap years). Combining `--month` with `--from` or `--to`, or specifying
  `--from` after `--to`, fails cleanly with the Error/Why/Fix triad. The stored ledger schema is
  unchanged; filtering operates on ISO-8601 string bounds during retrieval.
- **Consequences**: Users can analyze periodic spending without third-party tooling or spreadsheet
  exports. Backward compatibility is fully preserved for callers invoking `entries()` or `summary()`
  without date bounds.

"""Crash-safe file placement: temp file, fsync, atomic replace, directory fsync."""

import os
import shutil
import time
from pathlib import Path

REPLACE_TRIES = 5


def write_atomic(path: Path, data: bytes, keep_backup: bool = False) -> None:
    """Replace ``path`` with ``data`` so a power cut leaves the old or the new file, never half."""
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    tmp = path.with_name(f".tmp_{path.name}.{os.getpid()}")
    with open(tmp, "wb") as handle:
        handle.write(data)
        handle.flush()
        os.fsync(handle.fileno())
    if keep_backup and path.exists():
        shutil.copy2(path, path.with_name(path.name + ".bak"))
    replace_with_retry(tmp, path)
    fsync_dir(path.parent)


def replace_with_retry(src: Path, dst: Path) -> None:
    """os.replace, retried because Windows briefly locks files that a scanner has open."""
    for attempt in range(REPLACE_TRIES):
        try:
            os.replace(src, dst)
            return
        except PermissionError:
            if attempt == REPLACE_TRIES - 1:
                raise
            time.sleep(0.05 * (attempt + 1))


def fsync_dir(directory: Path) -> None:
    """Persist a directory entry; Windows cannot open a directory, and NTFS journals it anyway."""
    if os.name == "nt":
        return
    fd = os.open(directory, os.O_RDONLY)
    try:
        os.fsync(fd)
    finally:
        os.close(fd)

"""The SQLite file behind the catalog and the sync journal, with its format version."""

import sqlite3
import threading
from pathlib import Path

from .errors import HarborError

SCHEMA_VERSION = 1

_SCHEMA = """
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS photos (
    sha256 TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    rel_path TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    size INTEGER NOT NULL,
    original_name TEXT NOT NULL,
    media_type TEXT NOT NULL,
    taken_at TEXT,
    received_at TEXT NOT NULL,
    sort_time TEXT NOT NULL
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS photos_by_time ON photos (sort_time DESC, sha256 DESC);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS events (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    at TEXT NOT NULL,
    kind TEXT NOT NULL,
    sha256 TEXT,
    detail TEXT
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS events_by_kind ON events (kind, at);
"""


class Database:
    """One shared connection; every statement runs under ``lock`` so server threads take turns."""

    def __init__(self, path: Path) -> None:
        path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        self.lock = threading.RLock()
        self.conn = sqlite3.connect(path, check_same_thread=False, isolation_level=None)
        self.conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
        self.conn.execute("PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL")
        self.conn.execute("PRAGMA synchronous=FULL")
        self._open_schema(path)

    def _open_schema(self, path: Path) -> None:
        version = self.conn.execute("PRAGMA user_version").fetchone()[0]
        if version == 0:
            with self.lock:
                self.conn.executescript(_SCHEMA)
                self.conn.execute(f"PRAGMA user_version={SCHEMA_VERSION}")
        elif version != SCHEMA_VERSION:
            self.conn.close()
            raise HarborError(
                f"{path} uses catalog format {version}",
                f"this photo-harbor reads format {SCHEMA_VERSION} only",
                "run the photo-harbor version that created this library",
                status=500,
            )

    def close(self) -> None:
        with self.lock:
            self.conn.close()

"""What the phone did and when: uploads, finished syncs and photos the PC lacked at cleanup."""

from typing import Optional

from .database import Database

STORED = "stored"
DUPLICATE = "duplicate"
REJECTED = "rejected"
SYNC_DONE = "sync_done"
MISSING = "missing"


class SyncJournal:
    def __init__(self, db: Database) -> None:
        self._db = db

    def record(self, at: str, kind: str, sha256: Optional[str] = None,
               detail: Optional[str] = None) -> None:
        with self._db.lock:
            self._db.conn.execute(
                "INSERT INTO events (at, kind, sha256, detail) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)",
                (at, kind, sha256, detail),
            )

    def last_sync(self) -> Optional[str]:
        """The phone-reported start time of the latest sync that finished."""
        with self._db.lock:
            row = self._db.conn.execute(
                "SELECT detail FROM events WHERE kind = ? ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 1", (SYNC_DONE,)
            ).fetchone()
        return row[0] if row else None

    def counts_since(self, since: str) -> dict:
        with self._db.lock:
            rows = self._db.conn.execute(
                "SELECT kind, COUNT(*) FROM events WHERE at >= ? AND kind IN (?, ?, ?)"
                " GROUP BY kind",
                (since, STORED, DUPLICATE, REJECTED),
            ).fetchall()
        counts = {STORED: 0, DUPLICATE: 0, REJECTED: 0}
        counts.update({row[0]: row[1] for row in rows})
        return counts

    def missing(self, limit: int = 200) -> list:
        """Photos the phone holds that the PC still lacks, newest report first."""
        with self._db.lock:
            rows = self._db.conn.execute(
                "SELECT sha256, MAX(at) AS at, detail FROM events"
                " WHERE kind = ? AND sha256 NOT IN (SELECT sha256 FROM photos)"
                " GROUP BY sha256 ORDER BY at DESC LIMIT ?",
                (MISSING, limit),
            ).fetchall()
        return [{"sha256": row[0], "reported_at": row[1], "name": row[2]} for row in rows]

"""Receives originals, proves their bytes against the phone's hash, and re-proves them on request."""

import hashlib
import os
import re
import shutil
import threading
import uuid
from datetime import datetime
from pathlib import Path
from typing import BinaryIO, Callable, Optional

from .atomic_file import fsync_dir, replace_with_retry
from .catalog import Catalog
from .errors import HarborError
from .naming import media_type, month_folder, parse_taken, safe_name
from .records import IngestResult, PhotoRecord, UploadClaim

CHUNK = 1 << 20
MIN_FREE_BYTES = 10 * 1024 * 1024
MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES = 16 * 1024 ** 3
SHA256_HEX = re.compile(r"^[0-9a-f]{64}$")


def local_now() -> datetime:
    return datetime.now().astimezone()


def hash_file(path: Path) -> str:
    digest = hashlib.sha256()
    with open(path, "rb") as handle:
        for block in iter(lambda: handle.read(CHUNK), b""):
            digest.update(block)
    return digest.hexdigest()


def normalise_sha(value: Optional[str]) -> Optional[str]:
    """Lower-case hex, or HarborError when the text is not a SHA-256."""
    if value is None or value.strip() == "":
        return None
    cleaned = value.strip().lower()
    if not SHA256_HEX.match(cleaned):
        raise HarborError("the hash is not a SHA-256 hex string",
                          f"got {len(cleaned)} characters, expected 64 of 0-9a-f",
                          "set the Shortcut's Generate Hash action to SHA256")
    return cleaned


class PhotoStore:
    def __init__(self, library: Path, catalog: Catalog,
                 now: Callable[[], datetime] = local_now) -> None:
        self.photos_dir = library / "photos"
        self._incoming = library / ".harbor" / "incoming"
        self._catalog = catalog
        self._now = now
        self._place_lock = threading.Lock()
        self.photos_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        self._incoming.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        for stale in self._incoming.glob(".tmp_upload_*"):
            stale.unlink(missing_ok=True)

    def ingest(self, stream: BinaryIO, length: int, claim: UploadClaim) -> IngestResult:
        """Stream ``length`` bytes to disk; keep them only when the hash matches the claim."""
        expected = normalise_sha(claim.sha256)
        self._check_capacity(length)
        tmp = self._incoming / f".tmp_upload_{uuid.uuid4().hex}"
        try:
            actual = self._receive(stream, length, tmp)
            if expected is not None and actual != expected:
                raise HarborError("the photo arrived different from what the phone sent",
                                  "the SHA-256 of the received bytes does not match the phone's",
                                  "nothing was kept; the next sync sends it again", status=422)
            return self._place(tmp, actual, length, claim)
        finally:
            tmp.unlink(missing_ok=True)

    def verify(self, sha256: str) -> bool:
        """True only when the catalogued file exists and its bytes still hash to ``sha256``."""
        record = self._catalog.get(sha256)
        if record is None:
            return False
        path = self.photos_dir / record.rel_path
        try:
            if path.stat().st_size != record.size:
                return False
            return hash_file(path) == sha256
        except OSError:
            return False

    def locate(self, sha256: str) -> Optional[tuple]:
        """``(path, record)`` of a stored original, or None."""
        record = self._catalog.get(sha256)
        if record is None:
            return None
        path = self.photos_dir / record.rel_path
        return (path, record) if path.is_file() else None

    def _check_capacity(self, length: int) -> None:
        if length <= 0 or length > MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES:
            raise HarborError(f"an upload of {length} bytes was refused",
                              f"uploads must be 1 byte to {MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES} bytes",
                              "send the file as the request body with its Content-Length",
                              status=413 if length > 0 else 411)
        free = shutil.disk_usage(self._incoming).free
        if free < length + MIN_FREE_BYTES:
            raise HarborError("the PC's photo drive is full",
                              f"{free} bytes free, {length + MIN_FREE_BYTES} needed",
                              "free space on the library drive, then sync again", status=507)

    def _receive(self, stream: BinaryIO, length: int, tmp: Path) -> str:
        digest = hashlib.sha256()
        remaining = length
        with open(tmp, "wb") as handle:
            while remaining > 0:
                block = stream.read(min(CHUNK, remaining))
                if not block:
                    raise HarborError("the upload stopped early",
                                      f"{length - remaining} of {length} bytes arrived",
                                      "keep the phone on Wi-Fi; the next sync sends it again")
                digest.update(block)
                handle.write(block)
                remaining -= len(block)
            handle.flush()
            os.fsync(handle.fileno())
        return digest.hexdigest()

    def _place(self, tmp: Path, sha256: str, size: int, claim: UploadClaim) -> IngestResult:
        taken = parse_taken(claim.taken_at)
        received = self._now()
        name = safe_name(claim.original_name)
        with self._place_lock:
            existing = self._catalog.get(sha256)
            if existing is not None:
                return IngestResult("duplicate", existing)
            folder = self.photos_dir / month_folder(taken or received)
            folder.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            target = folder / name
            if target.exists():
                target = folder / f"{target.stem}-{sha256[:8]}{target.suffix}"
            replace_with_retry(tmp, target)
            fsync_dir(folder)
            record = PhotoRecord(
                sha256=sha256,
                rel_path=target.relative_to(self.photos_dir).as_posix(),
                size=size,
                original_name=claim.original_name[:255],
                media_type=media_type(name),
                taken_at=taken.isoformat(timespec="seconds") if taken else None,
                received_at=received.isoformat(timespec="seconds"),
            )
            self._catalog.add(record)
        return IngestResult("stored", record)

"""A throwaway library for tests: temp folder, database, catalog, journal and store."""

import hashlib
import io
import shutil
import tempfile
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

from photo_harbor.catalog import Catalog
from photo_harbor.database import Database
from photo_harbor.journal import SyncJournal
from photo_harbor.records import UploadClaim
from photo_harbor.store import PhotoStore

FIXED_NOW = datetime(2026, 10, 24, 12, 0, 0, tzinfo=timezone.utc)


def sha(data: bytes) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()


class Library:
    def __init__(self, test_case) -> None:
        self.root = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="harbor_test_"))
        test_case.addCleanup(shutil.rmtree, self.root, True)
        self.db = Database(self.root / ".harbor" / "catalog.sqlite3")
        test_case.addCleanup(self.db.close)
        self.catalog = Catalog(self.db)
        self.journal = SyncJournal(self.db)
        self.store = PhotoStore(self.root, self.catalog, now=lambda: FIXED_NOW)

    def put(self, data: bytes, name: str = "IMG_0001.HEIC", taken: str = None):
        claim = UploadClaim(original_name=name, sha256=sha(data), taken_at=taken)
        return self.store.ingest(io.BytesIO(data), len(data), claim)

import io
import unittest

from photo_harbor.database import Database
from photo_harbor.errors import HarborError
from photo_harbor.journal import MISSING, STORED, SYNC_DONE
from photo_harbor.records import UploadClaim
from tests.helpers import Library, sha


class IngestTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.lib = Library(self)

    def test_stores_under_the_month_it_was_taken(self):
        result = self.lib.put(b"photo-bytes", taken="2025-07-04T09:00:00")
        self.assertEqual(result.status, "stored")
        self.assertEqual(result.record.rel_path, "2025/07/IMG_0001.heic")
        self.assertEqual((self.lib.store.photos_dir / result.record.rel_path).read_bytes(),
                         b"photo-bytes")

    def test_same_bytes_twice_is_a_duplicate_and_keeps_one_file(self):
        self.lib.put(b"same")
        second = self.lib.put(b"same", name="copy.heic")
        self.assertEqual(second.status, "duplicate")
        self.assertEqual(self.lib.catalog.stats().count, 1)

    def test_a_name_clash_with_different_bytes_gets_a_hash_suffix(self):
        self.lib.put(b"first")
        second = self.lib.put(b"second")
        self.assertEqual(second.record.rel_path, f"2026/10/IMG_0001-{sha(b'second')[:8]}.heic")

    def test_hash_mismatch_keeps_nothing(self):
        claim = UploadClaim("IMG.HEIC", sha256=sha(b"what the phone hashed"))
        with self.assertRaises(HarborError) as caught:
            self.lib.store.ingest(io.BytesIO(b"something else"), 14, claim)
        self.assertEqual(caught.exception.status, 422)
        self.assertEqual(self.lib.catalog.stats().count, 0)
        self.assertEqual(list(self.lib.store.photos_dir.rglob("*.*")), [])

    def test_a_short_body_is_refused_and_leaves_no_temp_file(self):
        claim = UploadClaim("IMG.HEIC")
        with self.assertRaises(HarborError):
            self.lib.store.ingest(io.BytesIO(b"abc"), 10, claim)
        self.assertEqual(list((self.lib.root / ".harbor" / "incoming").iterdir()), [])

    def test_a_malformed_hash_is_a_usage_error(self):
        with self.assertRaises(HarborError) as caught:
            self.lib.store.ingest(io.BytesIO(b"x"), 1, UploadClaim("a.jpg", sha256="abc"))
        self.assertEqual(caught.exception.status, 400)


class VerifyTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.lib = Library(self)
        self.record = self.lib.put(b"original").record

    def test_an_intact_file_verifies(self):
        self.assertTrue(self.lib.store.verify(self.record.sha256))

    def test_an_unknown_hash_does_not(self):
        self.assertFalse(self.lib.store.verify(sha(b"never sent")))

    def test_a_changed_file_does_not(self):
        (self.lib.store.photos_dir / self.record.rel_path).write_bytes(b"0riginal")
        self.assertFalse(self.lib.store.verify(self.record.sha256))

    def test_a_deleted_file_does_not(self):
        (self.lib.store.photos_dir / self.record.rel_path).unlink()
        self.assertFalse(self.lib.store.verify(self.record.sha256))


class CatalogAndJournalTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.lib = Library(self)

    def test_page_is_newest_taken_first(self):
        self.lib.put(b"old", name="old.jpg", taken="2020-01-01T00:00:00")
        self.lib.put(b"new", name="new.jpg", taken="2024-01-01T00:00:00")
        names = [r.original_name for r in self.lib.catalog.page(0, 10)]
        self.assertEqual(names, ["new.jpg", "old.jpg"])

    def test_missing_report_clears_once_the_photo_arrives(self):
        digest = sha(b"late")
        self.lib.journal.record("2026-10-24T10:00:00", MISSING, digest, "IMG_9.HEIC")
        self.assertEqual([m["name"] for m in self.lib.journal.missing()], ["IMG_9.HEIC"])
        self.lib.put(b"late")
        self.assertEqual(self.lib.journal.missing(), [])

    def test_last_sync_and_counts(self):
        self.lib.journal.record("2026-10-24T10:00:00", STORED, "a" * 64)
        self.lib.journal.record("2026-10-24T10:05:00", SYNC_DONE, None, "2026-10-24T09:59:00")
        self.assertEqual(self.lib.journal.last_sync(), "2026-10-24T09:59:00")
        self.assertEqual(self.lib.journal.counts_since("2026-10-24")["stored"], 1)

    def test_an_unknown_catalog_version_is_refused_untouched(self):
        self.lib.db.conn.execute("PRAGMA user_version=99")
        path = self.lib.root / ".harbor" / "catalog.sqlite3"
        with self.assertRaises(HarborError):
            Database(path)

"""The endpoints the iPhone Shortcut calls: start, upload, done, and the cleanup's "has" check."""

from datetime import datetime, timedelta
from typing import Callable

from . import journal as kinds
from .errors import HarborError
from .journal import SyncJournal
from .messages import Reply, Request, json_reply
from .naming import parse_taken
from .records import UploadClaim
from .store import PhotoStore, local_now, normalise_sha

FIRST_SYNC_SINCE = "2000-01-01T00:00:00"
CLOCK_SLACK = timedelta(minutes=10)


def _stamp(moment: datetime) -> str:
    return moment.isoformat(timespec="seconds")


class SyncApi:
    def __init__(self, store: PhotoStore, journal: SyncJournal,
                 now: Callable[[], datetime] = local_now) -> None:
        self._store = store
        self._journal = journal
        self._now = now

    def start(self, request: Request) -> Reply:
        """Tell the phone which photos to send: those created after the last finished sync."""
        last = parse_taken(self._journal.last_sync())
        since = _stamp(last - CLOCK_SLACK) if last else FIRST_SYNC_SINCE
        return json_reply({"since": since, "started_at": _stamp(self._now())})

    def upload(self, request: Request) -> Reply:
        claim = UploadClaim(original_name=request.header("x-name", "photo"),
                            sha256=request.header("x-sha256") or None,
                            taken_at=request.header("x-taken") or None)
        try:
            result = self._store.ingest(request.body, request.length, claim)
        except HarborError as error:
            self._journal.record(_stamp(self._now()), kinds.REJECTED, None,
                                 f"{claim.original_name}: {error.message}")
            raise
        self._journal.record(_stamp(self._now()), result.status, result.record.sha256,
                             result.record.original_name)
        return json_reply({"status": result.status, "sha256": result.record.sha256,
                           "answer": "yes"})

    def has(self, request: Request) -> Reply:
        """``answer`` is ``yes`` only after the PC re-hashes its copy; a ``no`` is logged."""
        sha256 = normalise_sha(request.arg("sha256"))
        if sha256 is None:
            raise HarborError("no hash was given", "the check needs ?sha256=<64 hex characters>",
                              "pass the Generate Hash result in the URL")
        present = self._store.verify(sha256)
        if not present:
            self._journal.record(_stamp(self._now()), kinds.MISSING, sha256,
                                 request.arg("name", "")[:255] or None)
        return json_reply({"present": present, "answer": "yes" if present else "no"})

    def done(self, request: Request) -> Reply:
        started = str(request.json().get("started_at", ""))
        if parse_taken(started) is None:
            raise HarborError("the sync's start time is missing",
                              "`done` needs the started_at value that `start` returned",
                              "send {\"started_at\": <value from start>} as JSON")
        self._journal.record(_stamp(self._now()), kinds.SYNC_DONE, None, started)
        return json_reply({"ok": True})

"""Small JPEG previews, made only when the optional Pillow (and pillow-heif for HEIC) is installed."""

import io
import threading
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Optional

from .atomic_file import write_atomic
from .records import PhotoRecord

EDGE = 480
QUALITY = 82


def _load_pillow():
    """The Pillow Image module with HEIC support when available, or None without Pillow."""
    try:
        from PIL import Image, ImageOps
    except ImportError:
        return None
    try:
        from pillow_heif import register_heif_opener
        register_heif_opener()
    except ImportError:
        pass
    return Image, ImageOps


class Thumbnailer:
    def __init__(self, cache_dir: Path, pillow=_load_pillow) -> None:
        self._cache = cache_dir
        self._pillow = pillow()
        self._lock = threading.Lock()

    @property
    def enabled(self) -> bool:
        return self._pillow is not None

    def preview(self, record: PhotoRecord, original: Path) -> Optional[Path]:
        """The cached preview, made on first request; None for videos or unreadable images."""
        if self._pillow is None or record.is_video:
            return None
        target = self._cache / record.sha256[:2] / f"{record.sha256}.jpg"
        if target.exists():
            return target
        image_mod, ops = self._pillow
        try:
            with image_mod.open(original) as image:
                image = ops.exif_transpose(image).convert("RGB")
                image.thumbnail((EDGE, EDGE))
                buffer = io.BytesIO()
                image.save(buffer, "JPEG", quality=QUALITY, optimize=True)
        except Exception:  # hygiene: allow Pillow raises many types for unsupported formats
            return None
        with self._lock:
            write_atomic(target, buffer.getvalue())
        return target

"""Wires one library's storage, APIs and web page into a Router."""

from datetime import datetime
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Callable, Optional

from .auth import KeyGuard
from .catalog import Catalog
from .config import Settings
from .database import Database
from .errors import HarborError
from .journal import SyncJournal
from .library_api import LibraryApi
from .messages import Reply, Request
from .router import Router
from .setup_api import SetupApi
from .store import PhotoStore, local_now
from .sync_api import SyncApi
from .thumbs import Thumbnailer

WEB_DIR = Path(__file__).parent / "web"
STATIC_TYPES = {
    "index.html": "text/html; charset=utf-8",
    "app.css": "text/css; charset=utf-8",
    "app.js": "text/javascript; charset=utf-8",
    "icon.svg": "image/svg+xml",
    "manifest.webmanifest": "application/manifest+json",
}
NO_CACHE = (("Cache-Control", "no-cache"),)


def static_file(request: Request, name: str = "index.html") -> Reply:
    if name not in STATIC_TYPES:
        raise HarborError(f"no file {name}", "the gallery has no such asset", "open /", status=404)
    return Reply(200, content_type=STATIC_TYPES[name], headers=NO_CACHE, file=WEB_DIR / name)


class HarborApp:
    """Owns the database connection; ``close`` releases it."""

    def __init__(self, settings: Settings, port: int, thumbs: Optional[Thumbnailer] = None,
                 now: Callable[[], datetime] = local_now) -> None:
        self.db = Database(settings.state_dir / "catalog.sqlite3")
        catalog = Catalog(self.db)
        journal = SyncJournal(self.db)
        store = PhotoStore(settings.library, catalog, now)
        thumbs = thumbs or Thumbnailer(settings.state_dir / "thumbs")
        self.guard = KeyGuard(settings.key)
        self.router = Router()
        self._register(SyncApi(store, journal, now), LibraryApi(store, catalog, journal, thumbs, now),
                       SetupApi(settings.key, port))

    def _register(self, sync: SyncApi, library: LibraryApi, setup: SetupApi) -> None:
        add = self.router.add
        add("GET", "/", static_file, public=True)
        add("GET", "/static/", static_file, public=True)
        add("POST", "/api/login", self.guard.login, public=True)
        add("POST", "/api/sync/start", sync.start)
        add("POST", "/api/upload", sync.upload)
        add("POST", "/api/sync/done", sync.done)
        add("GET", "/api/has", sync.has)
        add("GET", "/api/status", library.status)
        add("GET", "/api/photos", library.photos)
        add("GET", "/api/setup", setup.details)
        add("GET", "/media/", library.media)
        add("GET", "/thumb/", library.thumb)

    def close(self) -> None:
        self.db.close()

"""The server over a real socket on 127.0.0.1, as the Shortcut and the gallery use it."""

import http.client
import json
import shutil
import tempfile
import threading
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

from photo_harbor.app import HarborApp
from photo_harbor.config import load_or_create
from photo_harbor.http_server import HarborServer
from tests.helpers import FIXED_NOW, sha


class _NoPreviews:
    enabled = False

    def preview(self, record, original):
        return None


class ServerTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        root = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="harbor_http_"))
        self.addCleanup(shutil.rmtree, root, True)
        self.settings = load_or_create(root)
        self.app = HarborApp(self.settings, port=0, thumbs=_NoPreviews(), now=lambda: FIXED_NOW)
        self.addCleanup(self.app.close)
        self.server = HarborServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), self.app.router, self.app.guard)
        thread = threading.Thread(target=self.server.serve_forever, kwargs={"poll_interval": 0.05})
        thread.start()
        self.addCleanup(thread.join)
        self.addCleanup(self.server.server_close)
        self.addCleanup(self.server.shutdown)

    def call(self, method, path, body=None, headers=None, key=True):
        conn = http.client.HTTPConnection("127.0.0.1", self.server.server_address[1], timeout=5)
        self.addCleanup(conn.close)
        sent = dict(headers or {})
        if key:
            sent["X-Harbor-Key"] = self.settings.key
        if isinstance(body, dict):
            body = json.dumps(body).encode()
            sent["Content-Type"] = "application/json"
        conn.request(method, path, body=body, headers=sent)
        response = conn.getresponse()
        return response, response.read()

    def upload(self, data, name="IMG_0001.HEIC", digest=None):
        headers = {"X-Name": name, "X-Sha256": digest or sha(data), "X-Taken": "2026-05-01T08:00:00Z"}
        return self.call("POST", "/api/upload", body=data, headers=headers)

    def test_a_full_sync_round(self):
        response, body = self.call("POST", "/api/sync/start", body={})
        start = json.loads(body)
        self.assertEqual(start["since"], "2000-01-01T00:00:00")
        response, body = self.upload(b"heic bytes")
        self.assertEqual((response.status, json.loads(body)["status"]), (200, "stored"))
        response, body = self.upload(b"heic bytes")
        self.assertEqual(json.loads(body)["status"], "duplicate")
        self.call("POST", "/api/sync/done", body={"started_at": start["started_at"]})
        _, body = self.call("POST", "/api/sync/start", body={})
        self.assertEqual(json.loads(body)["since"], "2026-10-24T11:50:00+00:00")

    def test_has_answers_yes_only_for_verified_photos(self):
        self.upload(b"kept")
        _, body = self.call("GET", f"/api/has?sha256={sha(b'kept')}")
        self.assertEqual(json.loads(body)["answer"], "yes")
        _, body = self.call("GET", f"/api/has?sha256={sha(b'not sent')}&name=IMG_7.HEIC")
        self.assertEqual(json.loads(body)["answer"], "no")
        _, body = self.call("GET", "/api/status")
        self.assertEqual([m["name"] for m in json.loads(body)["missing"]], ["IMG_7.HEIC"])

    def test_a_mismatched_hash_is_rejected_and_counted(self):
        response, body = self.upload(b"actual", digest=sha(b"claimed"))
        self.assertEqual(response.status, 422)
        self.assertIn("why", json.loads(body))
        _, body = self.call("GET", "/api/status")
        self.assertEqual(json.loads(body)["last_day"]["rejected"], 1)

    def test_calls_without_the_key_are_refused_but_the_page_loads(self):
        response, _ = self.call("GET", "/api/status", key=False)
        self.assertEqual(response.status, 401)
        response, body = self.call("GET", "/", key=False)
        self.assertEqual(response.status, 200)
        self.assertIn(b"<html", body)

    def test_login_sets_a_cookie_that_opens_the_api(self):
        response, _ = self.call("POST", "/api/login", body={"key": self.settings.key}, key=False)
        cookie = response.getheader("Set-Cookie").split(";", 1)[0]
        response, _ = self.call("GET", "/api/status", headers={"Cookie": cookie}, key=False)
        self.assertEqual(response.status, 200)

    def test_media_serves_ranges_for_video_scrubbing(self):
        self.upload(b"0123456789", name="clip.MOV")
        response, body = self.call("GET", f"/media/{sha(b'0123456789')}", headers={"Range": "bytes=2-4"})
        self.assertEqual((response.status, body), (206, b"234"))
        self.assertEqual(response.getheader("Content-Type"), "video/quicktime")

    def test_photos_lists_newest_first_with_paging(self):
        self.upload(b"a", name="a.jpg")
        self.upload(b"b", name="b.jpg")
        _, body = self.call("GET", "/api/photos?limit=1")
        page = json.loads(body)
        self.assertEqual((len(page["photos"]), page["next"]), (1, 1))

    def test_a_chunked_upload_is_accepted(self):
        data = b"chunked photo"
        framed = b"%x\r\n%s\r\n0\r\n\r\n" % (len(data), data)
        headers = {"X-Name": "c.jpg", "X-Sha256": sha(data), "Transfer-Encoding": "chunked"}
        response, body = self.call("POST", "/api/upload", body=framed, headers=headers)
        self.assertEqual((response.status, json.loads(body)["status"]), (200, "stored"))

    1 · Two values for the Shortcut

    Server–

    Send both to the iPhone (AirDrop or a note) so they can be pasted, not typed.

    2 · Shortcut “Harbor Sync”

    In the Shortcuts app tap +, name it Harbor Sync and add these actions in order.

    1. Get Network Details → Wi-Fi, Network Name. Then If Network Details is not your home Wi-Fi name → Stop This Shortcut. End If.
    2. Get Contents of URL [Server]/api/sync/start. Method POST, header X-Harbor-Key = [Key]. Then Get Dictionary Value since → Get Dates from Input → Set Variable Since. Get Dictionary Value started_at from the same result → Set Variable StartedAt.
    3. Find Photos where Creation Date is after Since, sorted by Creation Date, oldest first.
    4. Repeat with Each item in Photos:
      1. Generate Hash SHA256 of Repeat Item → Set Variable Hash.
      2. Get Contents of URL [Server]/api/has?sha256=[Hash] (GET, same key header) → Get Dictionary Value answer.
      3. If answer is not yes: Get Name of Repeat Item; Format Date Creation Date of Repeat Item as ISO 8601; Get Contents of URL [Server]/api/upload, POST, headers X-Harbor-Key = [Key], X-Name = Name, X-Sha256 = Hash, X-Taken = Formatted Date, Request Body File = Repeat Item. Get Dictionary Value answer; If it is not yes → Add to Variable Failures.
    5. If Failures does not have any value → Get Contents of URL [Server]/api/sync/done, POST, same key header, Request Body JSON started_at = StartedAt.

    If anything failed, the sync is not marked done, so the next run tries those photos again. Photos already on the PC are only hashed, not re-sent.

    3 · Run it automatically

    Shortcuts → Automation → + → choose the trigger → Run Immediately → Harbor Sync.

    • Wi-Fi: your home network. Runs when she gets home.
    • Charger: is connected. Sends what she took while already at home.
    • Time of Day (optional): e.g. 12:00, 18:00 and 22:00.

    4 · Shortcut “Harbor Cleanup” (free up space)

    1. The same Wi-Fi check as step 1.

    3. Repeat with Each: Generate Hash SHA256; Get Name; Get Contents of URL [Server]/api/has?sha256=[Hash]&name=[Name]&report=1; Get Dictionary Value answer. If answer is yes → Add to Variable Safe. Otherwise → the same upload request as in Harbor Sync (it is kept on the phone this time).

"""A second copy of the library's originals on another drive, so one disk failure loses nothing."""

import os
import shutil
import threading
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path

from .atomic_file import replace_with_retry
from .errors import HarborError

DAY_SECONDS = 24 * 3600


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class BackupReport:
    copied: int
    unchanged: int
    bytes_copied: int


def mirror(source: Path, target: Path) -> BackupReport:
    """Copy each original missing from ``target`` or differing in size; never deletes there."""
    if target.resolve() == source.resolve() or source.resolve() in target.resolve().parents:
        raise HarborError(f"{target} is inside the library",
                          "a backup in the same folder dies with the same disk",
                          "choose a folder on another drive, e.g. E:\\HarborBackup")
    copied = unchanged = total = 0
    for path in sorted(source.rglob("*")):
        if not path.is_file():
            continue
        dest = target / path.relative_to(source)
        size = path.stat().st_size
        if dest.is_file() and dest.stat().st_size == size:
            unchanged += 1
            continue
        dest.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        tmp = dest.with_name(f".tmp_{dest.name}")
        shutil.copyfile(path, tmp)
        with open(tmp, "rb+") as handle:
            os.fsync(handle.fileno())
        replace_with_retry(tmp, dest)
        copied += 1
        total += size
    return BackupReport(copied, unchanged, total)


class DailyBackup:
    """Mirrors at start-up and every 24 hours on a background thread while the server runs."""

    def __init__(self, source: Path, target: Path, log=print) -> None:
        self._source = source
        self._target = target
        self._log = log
        self._stop = threading.Event()
        self._thread = threading.Thread(target=self._run, name="harbor-backup", daemon=True)

    def start(self) -> None:
        self._thread.start()

    def stop(self) -> None:
        self._stop.set()
        self._thread.join(timeout=5)

    def _run(self) -> None:
        while not self._stop.is_set():
            try:
                report = mirror(self._source, self._target)
                self._log(f"Backup: {report.copied} copied, {report.unchanged} already there "
                          f"-> {self._target}")
            except (OSError, HarborError) as error:
                self._log(f"Backup failed: {error}. It retries in 24 hours.")
            self._stop.wait(DAY_SECONDS)

"""Command line: ``python -m photo_harbor serve | key | backup``."""

import argparse
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from . import __version__
from .errors import HarborError

DEFAULT_LIBRARY = Path.home() / "Pictures" / "Harbor"
DEFAULT_PORT = 8642


def _parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="python -m photo_harbor",
                                     description="A photo server an iPhone feeds over home Wi-Fi.")
    parser.add_argument("--version", action="version", version=__version__)
    parser.add_argument("--library", type=Path, default=DEFAULT_LIBRARY,
                        help=f"folder that holds the photos (default: {DEFAULT_LIBRARY})")
    commands = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
    serve = commands.add_parser("serve", help="run the server and gallery")
    serve.add_argument("--port", type=int, default=DEFAULT_PORT, help=f"default {DEFAULT_PORT}")
    serve.add_argument("--host", default="0.0.0.0", help="address to listen on (default: all)")
    serve.add_argument("--backup-to", type=Path, help="mirror originals here daily (another drive)")
    key = commands.add_parser("key", help="print the key the Shortcut sends")
    key.add_argument("--new", action="store_true", help="replace it; old Shortcuts stop working")
    backup = commands.add_parser("backup", help="copy originals to another drive once")
    backup.add_argument("--to", type=Path, required=True, help="backup folder")
    return parser


def _serve(args, settings) -> int:
    from .app import HarborApp
    from .backup import DailyBackup
    from .http_server import HarborServer
    from .setup_api import lan_address

    app = HarborApp(settings, args.port)
    try:
        server = HarborServer((args.host, args.port), app.router, app.guard)
    except OSError as exc:
        app.close()
        raise HarborError(f"port {args.port} is not available", str(exc),
                          "close the other Harbor window, or pass --port 8643") from exc
    backup = DailyBackup(settings.library / "photos", args.backup_to) if args.backup_to else None
    print(f"Harbor {__version__} is running. Press Ctrl+C to stop.")
    print(f"  Library:   {settings.library}")
    print(f"  This PC:   http://localhost:{args.port}")
    print(f"  iPhone:    http://{lan_address()}:{args.port}")
    print(f"  Key:       {settings.key}")
    print(f"  Backup:    {args.backup_to or 'off (add --backup-to E:\\HarborBackup)'}")
    if backup:
        backup.start()
    try:
        server.serve_forever()
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        print("Stopping.")
    finally:
        server.server_close()
        if backup:
            backup.stop()
        app.close()
    return 0


def main(argv=None) -> int:
    args = _parser().parse_args(argv)
    from .config import load_or_create, rotate_key

    try:
        library = args.library.expanduser().resolve()
        if args.command == "key":
            settings = rotate_key(library) if args.new else load_or_create(library)
            print(settings.key)
            return 0
        if args.command == "backup":
            from .backup import mirror
            report = mirror(library / "photos", args.to.expanduser().resolve())
            print(f"Copied {report.copied} ({report.bytes_copied} bytes); "
                  f"{report.unchanged} already backed up.")
            return 0
        return _serve(args, load_or_create(library))
    except HarborError as error:
        print(error.as_text(), file=sys.stderr)
        return 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

import io
import json
import shutil
import tempfile
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

from photo_harbor.auth import is_home_network
from photo_harbor.backup import mirror
from photo_harbor.body_readers import ChunkedReader, LengthReader
from photo_harbor.config import load_or_create, rotate_key
from photo_harbor.errors import HarborError
from photo_harbor.messages import Request, parse_range
from photo_harbor.router import Router


def temp_dir(test_case) -> Path:
    path = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="harbor_parts_"))
    test_case.addCleanup(shutil.rmtree, path, True)
    return path


class RangeTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_closed_open_and_suffix_ranges(self):
        self.assertEqual(parse_range("bytes=2-4", 10), (2, 4))
        self.assertEqual(parse_range("bytes=7-", 10), (7, 9))
        self.assertEqual(parse_range("bytes=-3", 10), (7, 9))

    def test_unsatisfiable_or_multiple_ranges_mean_the_whole_file(self):
        self.assertIsNone(parse_range("bytes=12-20", 10))
        self.assertIsNone(parse_range("bytes=0-1,4-5", 10))
        self.assertIsNone(parse_range("items=0-1", 10))


class BodyReaderTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_length_reader_stops_at_the_length(self):
        reader = LengthReader(io.BytesIO(b"abcdef"), 4)
        self.assertEqual(reader.read(), b"abcd")
        self.assertTrue(reader.exhausted)

    def test_chunked_reader_decodes_and_consumes_the_trailer(self):
        raw = io.BytesIO(b"3\r\nabc\r\n2;ext=1\r\nde\r\n0\r\n\r\nNEXT")
        reader = ChunkedReader(raw)
        self.assertEqual(reader.read(10) + reader.read(10) + reader.read(10), b"abcde")
        self.assertTrue(reader.exhausted)
        self.assertEqual(raw.read(), b"NEXT")

    def test_json_body_must_be_an_object(self):
        request = Request("POST", "/", body=io.BytesIO(b"[1]"), length=3)
        with self.assertRaises(HarborError):
            request.json()


class RouterTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_exact_and_prefix_routes(self):
        router = Router()
        router.add("GET", "/", "index", public=True)
        router.add("GET", "/media/", "media")
        self.assertEqual(router.match("GET", "/").handler, "index")
        self.assertEqual(router.match("GET", "/media/abc").param, "abc")
        self.assertIsNone(router.match("GET", "/media/a/b"))
        self.assertIsNone(router.match("POST", "/media/abc"))


class HomeNetworkTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_private_addresses_are_home(self):
        for address in ("192.168.1.20", "10.0.0.5", "127.0.0.1", "::ffff:192.168.1.9", "fe80::1%12"):
            self.assertTrue(is_home_network(address), address)

    def test_public_addresses_are_not(self):
        self.assertFalse(is_home_network("8.8.8.8"))
        self.assertFalse(is_home_network("not an ip"))


class ConfigTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_first_run_creates_a_key_that_later_runs_reuse(self):
        library = temp_dir(self)
        first = load_or_create(library)
        self.assertGreaterEqual(len(first.key), 16)
        self.assertEqual(load_or_create(library).key, first.key)

    def test_a_damaged_file_is_restored_from_its_backup(self):
        library = temp_dir(self)
        rotate_key(library)
        second = rotate_key(library)
        config = library / ".harbor" / "config.json"
        config.write_text("{broken", encoding="utf-8")
        restored = load_or_create(library)
        self.assertNotEqual(restored.key, second.key)
        self.assertTrue((library / ".harbor" / "config.json.corrupt").exists())

    def test_an_unknown_version_is_refused_without_touching_the_file(self):
        library = temp_dir(self)
        config = library / ".harbor" / "config.json"
        config.parent.mkdir(parents=True)
        config.write_text(json.dumps({"version": 9, "key": "x" * 20}), encoding="utf-8")
        with self.assertRaises(HarborError):
            load_or_create(library)
        self.assertEqual(json.loads(config.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))["version"], 9)


class BackupTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_copies_new_files_and_skips_ones_already_there(self):
        root = temp_dir(self)
        source, target = root / "photos", root / "backup"
        (source / "2026" / "10").mkdir(parents=True)
        (source / "2026" / "10" / "a.heic").write_bytes(b"aaa")
        first = mirror(source, target)
        second = mirror(source, target)
        self.assertEqual((first.copied, second.copied, second.unchanged), (1, 0, 1))
        self.assertEqual((target / "2026" / "10" / "a.heic").read_bytes(), b"aaa")

    def test_refuses_a_target_inside_the_library(self):
        root = temp_dir(self)
        with self.assertRaises(HarborError):
            mirror(root, root / "inside")

# photo-harbor

[![Built with AIKit](https://img.shields.io/badge/built%20with-AIKit-6f42c1)](https://github.com/Aegean-E/AIKit)

Self-hosted photo server for Windows: an iPhone sends new photos over home Wi-Fi through Apple Shortcuts, no app needed, with a verified-hash cleanup and a gallery.

## ⚡ 30-Second Cold-Start Quick Reference

- **Runtime Prerequisites**: Python 3.10 or newer (standard library only). Optional: `pip install pillow pillow-heif` for HEIC thumbnails in every browser.
- **Canonical Regression Shield Gate**:
  ```bash
  python -m unittest discover -s tests -t .
  ```
- **Try it now** (from this folder):
  ```bash
  python -m photo_harbor serve
  ```
  Open `http://localhost:8642` and sign in with the key it prints. When Windows Firewall asks,
  allow Python on **Private networks** so the iPhone can reach it.

### 🛠️ AIKit Commands (run from the AIKit folder)
| Role | Command |
|---|---|
| Status, task and gates | `python aikit.py status photo-harbor` |
| Phase 4: every gate | `python aikit.py check photo-harbor` |
| Repair memory and map, then check | `python aikit.py fix photo-harbor` |
| Resume an interrupted task | `python aikit.py resume photo-harbor` |

## 💡 How It Works

- **No iPhone app.** Two Shortcuts built in Apple's Shortcuts app call the server. The gallery's
  **Setup** tab lists every action, with the server address and key ready to copy.
- **Automatic on home Wi-Fi.** Automations run *Harbor Sync* when the phone joins the home
  network and when it is plugged in. The Shortcut stops at once on any other network.
- **Only what is new is sent.** `POST /api/sync/start` returns the time of the last finished
  sync (minus 10 minutes of clock slack). The Shortcut asks `GET /api/has` before each upload,
  so photos already on the PC are only hashed, never re-sent. The sync is marked done only if
  every upload succeeded.
- **Every byte is proven.** The phone sends the SHA-256 of each file with it. The PC streams the
  upload to a temporary file, hashes it, and keeps it only if the hashes match. Then it fsyncs
  the file and moves it into `photos/YYYY/MM/` under its original name. A name clash with different
  bytes gets a hash suffix; identical bytes are stored once.
- **Deletion only after a fresh check.** *Harbor Cleanup* asks `GET /api/has` for each phone photo
  older than 30 days. The PC answers `yes` only after re-hashing its own copy. Only those photos
  are deleted, and iOS asks once to confirm. A `no` uploads the photo instead and appears under
  **Sync → On the iPhone, not yet on the PC** until it arrives.
- **Home network only.** Requests from public IP addresses are refused even if a router forwards
  the port. Every API call needs the library key, sent as `X-Harbor-Key` or by the gallery's
  sign-in cookie.
- **Second copy.** `--backup-to E:\HarborBackup` mirrors the originals at start-up and every 24
  hours. It never deletes anything in the backup.

### Commands

```text
python -m photo_harbor [--library DIR] serve [--port 8642] [--host 0.0.0.0] [--backup-to DIR]
python -m photo_harbor [--library DIR] key [--new]      # print, or replace, the Shortcut key
python -m photo_harbor [--library DIR] backup --to DIR  # one-off mirror to another drive
```

The default library is `%USERPROFILE%\Pictures\Harbor`. Errors print `Error:`, `Why:` and `Fix:`
and exit 1; usage errors exit 2.

### HTTP API

| Call | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `POST /api/sync/start` | `{since, started_at}`: which photos to send |
| `POST /api/upload` | raw file body; headers `X-Name`, `X-Sha256`, `X-Taken`. `{status: stored\|duplicate, answer: yes}` |
| `GET /api/has?sha256=…[&name=…&report=1]` | `{present, answer: yes\|no}` after re-hashing the PC's copy |
| `POST /api/sync/done` | JSON `{started_at}`: records a finished sync |
| `GET /api/status`, `GET /api/photos?offset=&limit=` | gallery data |
| `GET /media/<sha256>`, `GET /thumb/<sha256>` | original (with byte ranges) and JPEG preview |

## 📦 What's Inside

```text
photo-harbor/
├── .aikit/                   <- this project's memory: record, ledger, decisions
├── .gitignore
├── LICENSE                   <- GNU AGPL-3.0
├── README.md
├── photo_harbor/
│   ├── __main__.py           <- `python -m photo_harbor` commands
│   ├── app.py                <- wires storage, APIs and the web page into routes
│   ├── atomic_file.py        <- temp + fsync + replace placement
│   ├── auth.py               <- home-network check, key and sign-in cookie
│   ├── backup.py             <- mirror to a second drive, daily thread
│   ├── body_readers.py       <- Content-Length and chunked request bodies
│   ├── catalog.py            <- index of stored originals by SHA-256
│   ├── config.py             <- settings file with the library key
│   ├── database.py           <- SQLite file and its format version
│   ├── errors.py             <- the Error/Why/Fix triad
│   ├── http_server.py        <- HTTP handling, byte ranges, security headers
│   ├── journal.py            <- uploads, finished syncs, photos reported missing
│   ├── library_api.py        <- status, photo list, originals, previews
│   ├── messages.py           <- Request and Reply values, Range parsing
│   ├── naming.py             <- safe file names, month folders, media types
│   ├── records.py            <- frozen value objects
│   ├── router.py             <- method + path routing
│   ├── setup_api.py          <- address and key for the Setup tab
│   ├── store.py              <- hash-verified ingest and re-verification
│   ├── sync_api.py           <- the endpoints the Shortcuts call
│   ├── thumbs.py             <- optional Pillow previews
│   └── web/                  <- gallery: index.html, app.css, app.js, icon, manifest
└── tests/
    ├── library_fixture.py    <- a throwaway library for tests
    ├── test_http.py          <- the server over a real socket
    ├── test_naming.py
    ├── test_parts.py
    └── test_store.py
```

Library layout: `photos/YYYY/MM/<original name>` holds the originals untouched;
`.harbor/` holds `config.json`, `catalog.sqlite3`, `incoming/` and `thumbs/`.

## ⚠️ Limits

- The PC must be on, awake and on the same Wi-Fi.
- iOS always asks before Shortcuts deletes photos. Deleted photos stay in *Recently Deleted* for
  30 days. With iCloud Photos on, deleting also removes them from iCloud.
- Very large videos may need more than one run because Shortcuts limits how long one run takes.
- Thumbnails need Pillow. Without them, Safari still shows HEIC originals; other browsers show a
  placeholder.

### ADR-001: Apple Shortcuts as the phone client, hash-proven ingest, SQLite catalog
- **Date**: 2026-10-24
- **Status**: Accepted
- **Context**: The user wants an iPhone to copy photos to their Windows PC whenever it is on the
  home Wi-Fi, with no app installed, and to delete from the phone only what the PC really holds.
  A web page cannot read the photo library in the background; Shortcuts automations can.
- **Decision**: The phone side is two Shortcuts (sync and cleanup) documented in the gallery's
  Setup tab, since unsigned `.shortcut` files cannot be imported on current iOS. The server is
  Python standard library only (`http.server`, `sqlite3`). Each upload carries the phone's
  SHA-256; the server streams to `.harbor/incoming`, hashes, keeps the file only on a match,
  fsyncs and `os.replace`s it into `photos/YYYY/MM/`. `GET /api/has` re-hashes the stored copy
  before answering `yes`. The catalog and journal live in one SQLite file (WAL,
  `synchronous=FULL`, `PRAGMA user_version` 1, unknown versions refused untouched), so
  transactions replace the temp-file-and-replace protocol for that state. `config.json` uses
  the atomic write with a `.bak`. Requests from non-private addresses are refused, and every API
  call needs the library key. Pillow and pillow-heif are optional and imported only in
  `thumbs.py`.
- **Consequences**: Nothing is installed on the iPhone and nothing unverified can be deleted. The
  cost is a manual Shortcut setup (about ten minutes), one confirmation tap per cleanup (iOS
  enforces it), and a full re-hash per `has` query, which is slow for large videos. If
  Shortcuts' Generate Hash ever hashes different bytes than it uploads, every upload is
  rejected (422) rather than stored unverified.
EOF

content.text:
I've built Harbor, the photo server, as a new project in [projects/photo-harbor](projects/photo-harbor). It works on the PC side, but **I couldn't test it with an iPhone**, so the Shortcuts part is still unproven.

**What I checked:** all 45 automated tests and the project's 4 quality checks pass. I also ran the real server and uploaded a test photo: it was stored in `photos/2026/10/`, confirmed by its fingerprint, and got a thumbnail. Every gallery file loaded. I did not open the gallery in a browser, so I haven't seen how it actually looks.

**To start it on your PC:**
```
cd projects/photo-harbor
python -m photo_harbor serve --backup-to E:\HarborBackup
```
- **Backup drive:** use your second drive's letter, or leave out `--backup-to` if you don't have one. The backup copy runs when the server starts and every 24 hours after that.
- **Window:** it prints the iPhone address and the key. Leave it running.
- **Firewall:** when Windows Firewall asks, allow Python on **Private networks**. Your home Wi-Fi also needs to be set as a Private network in Windows.
- **Photo folder:** photos go to `Pictures\Harbor\photos\YYYY\MM\`, keeping their original files and names.
- **Thumbnails:** Pillow is installed here, but `pillow-heif` probably isn't. Without it, iPhone (HEIC) photos get no thumbnails in Chrome or Edge on the PC; Safari on the iPhone still shows them. `pip install pillow-heif` fixes that.

**On the iPhone:** open `http://<pc-ip>:8642` in Safari and sign in with the key. The **Setup** tab lists every Shortcut action step by step, with the address and key ready to copy. Then she can add it to her home screen. One change from what I promised: there's no Shortcut file to import, because current iOS blocks importing unsigned ones. Building the two Shortcuts by hand takes about 10 minutes.

**What the iPhone test will tell us:** the whole design assumes the Shortcut fingerprints exactly the bytes it uploads. If that's not true, the PC will refuse every photo (error 422) rather than store anything unconfirmed, and nothing gets deleted. The **Sync** tab counts these refusals as "failed", so you'll see it straight away. If it happens, I'll need to adjust the Shortcut steps.

"""Seed a demo library, serve it, and screenshot the gallery with Playwright (Edge)."""
import hashlib, io, math, random, shutil, sys, threading
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
from pathlib import Path

PROJECT = Path(r"C:\Users\Yunus-Emre\Desktop\portable_agent_kit\projects\photo-harbor")
sys.path.insert(0, str(PROJECT))
from PIL import Image, ImageDraw, ImageFilter  # noqa: E402
from photo_harbor.app import HarborApp  # noqa: E402
from photo_harbor.config import load_or_create  # noqa: E402
from photo_harbor.http_server import HarborServer  # noqa: E402
from photo_harbor.records import UploadClaim  # noqa: E402

HERE = Path(__file__).parent
LIB = HERE / "demo_lib"
OUT = HERE / "shots"
PORT = 8711
PALETTES = [((242, 166, 90), (90, 60, 120)), ((120, 190, 220), (20, 60, 110)), ((250, 220, 180), (200, 90, 80)),
            ((140, 200, 140), (30, 80, 60)), ((230, 230, 240), (120, 130, 160)), ((255, 190, 200), (120, 70, 140))]


def picture(seed):
    rnd = random.Random(seed)
    a, b = rnd.choice(PALETTES)
    w, h = rnd.choice([(900, 1200), (1200, 900), (1000, 1000)])
    img = Image.new("RGB", (w, h))
    px = ImageDraw.Draw(img)
    for y in range(h):
        t = y / h
        px.line([(0, y), (w, y)], fill=tuple(int(a[i] * (1 - t) + b[i] * t) for i in range(3)))
    for _ in range(5):
        r = rnd.randint(60, 260); x = rnd.randint(0, w); y = rnd.randint(0, h)
        px.ellipse([x - r, y - r, x + r, y + r], fill=tuple(min(255, c + rnd.randint(-40, 60)) for c in a))
    img = img.filter(ImageFilter.GaussianBlur(18))
    buf = io.BytesIO(); img.save(buf, "JPEG", quality=85)
    return buf.getvalue()


def seed(app_store):
    now = datetime(2026, 10, 24, 18, 0)
    n = 0
    for day in [0, 0, 1, 3, 9, 20, 41, 70, 130, 200, 380]:
        for k in range(random.Random(day).randint(2, 9)):
            data = picture(day * 100 + k)
            taken = (now - timedelta(days=day, minutes=k * 17)).isoformat()
            app_store.ingest(io.BytesIO(data), len(data), UploadClaim(f"IMG_{4000 + n}.JPG", hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest(), taken))
            n += 1
    print("seeded", n)


def main():
    fresh = "--fresh" in sys.argv
    if fresh and LIB.exists():
        shutil.rmtree(LIB)
    settings = load_or_create(LIB)
    app = HarborApp(settings, PORT)
    if fresh:
        from photo_harbor.catalog import Catalog
        from photo_harbor.store import PhotoStore
        seed(PhotoStore(LIB, Catalog(app.db)))
    server = HarborServer(("127.0.0.1", PORT), app.router, app.guard, verbose=False)
    threading.Thread(target=server.serve_forever, daemon=True).start()
    from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright
    tag = next((a.split("=", 1)[1] for a in sys.argv if a.startswith("--tag=")), "now")
    with sync_playwright() as p:
        browser = p.chromium.launch(channel="msedge")
        for name, viewport, scheme, mobile in [("desktop", {"width": 1366, "height": 860}, "light", False),
                                               ("desktop-dark", {"width": 1366, "height": 860}, "dark", False),
                                               ("phone", {"width": 390, "height": 844}, "light", True)]:
            ctx = browser.new_context(viewport=viewport, color_scheme=scheme, device_scale_factor=2 if mobile else 1,
                                      is_mobile=mobile, has_touch=mobile)
            page = ctx.new_page()
            errors = []
            page.on("console", lambda m: errors.append(m.text) if m.type == "error" else None)
            page.on("pageerror", lambda e: errors.append(str(e)))
            page.goto(f"http://127.0.0.1:{PORT}/")
            page.wait_for_timeout(400)
            if name == "desktop":
                page.screenshot(path=str(OUT / f"{tag}-login.png"))
            page.fill("#login-key", settings.key)
            page.click("#login-form button")
            page.wait_for_timeout(1200)
            page.screenshot(path=str(OUT / f"{tag}-{name}.png"))
            for view in ("sync", "setup"):
                if name != "phone":
                    page.click(f"[data-view={view}]"); page.wait_for_timeout(400)
                    page.screenshot(path=str(OUT / f"{tag}-{name}-{view}.png"))
            extra = [a for a in sys.argv if a.startswith("--do=")]
            for step in extra:
                exec(step.split("=", 1)[1], {"page": page, "OUT": OUT, "tag": tag, "name": name})
            print(name, "errors:", errors or "none")
            ctx.close()
        browser.close()
    server.shutdown(); app.close()


main()

"""The capture time stored inside a photo, for uploads that arrive without one (browser uploads)."""

import importlib.util
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Optional

DATETIME_ORIGINAL = 0x9003
EXIF_IFD = 0x8769
DATETIME = 0x0132


def read_taken(path: Path) -> Optional[str]:
    """``YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS`` from EXIF DateTimeOriginal, or None without Pillow or a date."""
    if importlib.util.find_spec("PIL") is None:
        return None
    from PIL import Image
    if importlib.util.find_spec("pillow_heif") is not None:
        from pillow_heif import register_heif_opener
        register_heif_opener()
    try:
        # hygiene: allow Pillow's Image.open reads binary image data, not text
        with Image.open(path) as image:
            exif = image.getexif()
            value = exif.get_ifd(EXIF_IFD).get(DATETIME_ORIGINAL) or exif.get(DATETIME)
    except Exception:  # hygiene: allow Pillow raises many types for files it cannot parse
        return None
    if not isinstance(value, str) or len(value) < 19:
        return None
    return f"{value[0:4]}-{value[5:7]}-{value[8:10]}T{value[11:19]}"

### ADR-002: Month/kind/name browsing and hashless browser uploads
- **Date**: 2026-10-24
- **Status**: Accepted
- **Context**: The user wants to browse the library on the web, not only scroll a single
  timeline, and a way to add photos from a browser. Review screenshots also showed unfinished
  rows with clipped corners, "Today" in English beside dates in the browser's language, and
  setup panels hugging the left edge.
- **Decision**: `GET /api/outline` returns months with counts and the video count;
  `GET /api/photos` takes `month`, `kind` and `q` (a LIKE match on the original name, with `!` as
  the escape character). The gallery shows these as a sticky sidebar, which becomes a chip row
  under 900 px. Search spans the whole library. `POST /api/upload` accepts a percent-encoded
  `X-Name` and no `X-Sha256`: the PC hashes what it received, so a browser upload is proven
  against its own bytes, not a phone's. The date order is `X-Taken`, then EXIF DateTimeOriginal
  via optional Pillow (`exif_dates.py`, injected into `PhotoStore`), then `X-Modified`. Tiles are
  rounded individually, today/yesterday come from `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat`, and the Sync and
  Setup views are centred at 920 px.
- **Consequences**: Browser uploads skip the end-to-end hash check that Shortcut uploads get. A
  dropped connection is still caught by the Content-Length check, and the cleanup only deletes
  what `has` re-verifies. Without Pillow, browser-uploaded photos are dated by their file time,
  which on an iPhone picker can be the time they were picked.
EOF
